content.title: About
content.content: Lo mein is a classic Chinese stir‑fried noodle dish made from wheat flour noodles. This version features tender strips of pork, mixed vegetables, and a savory soy‑based sauce, creating a flavorful and satisfying meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lo mein originated in China in the early 20th century as a popular street‑food dish.
Traditionally the noodles are hand‑pulled, but most modern restaurants use pre‑made dried noodles for convenience.
Pork is usually sliced thin and quickly stir‑fried to stay juicy.
The dish is often garnished with scallions, carrots, and bean sprouts for added texture and taste.
A Japanese counterpart called “yaki udon” uses a sweeter sauce but follows a similar preparation method.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Both pork and wheat noodles provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Pork supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish contains B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Carbohydrates for energy
items.content: Noodles deliver quick‑release carbs, making the meal a good pre‑exercise option.

items.title: Antioxidants from vegetables
items.content: Added vegetables such as carrots and bean sprouts provide vitamins A and C and other antioxidants.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce can be very salty; people with hypertension should limit the amount used.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat noodles contain gluten, making the dish unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

items.title: Pork fat
items.content: Some cuts of pork are fatty; choosing lean cuts or trimming excess fat reduces saturated fat intake.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to soy should substitute the sauce with a soy‑free alternative.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve lo mein hot, tossing the noodles with sauce and pork. It is typically eaten with a fork or chopsticks, cutting larger pork pieces as needed. A squeeze of lime or a sprinkle of fresh cilantro adds brightness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The dish is best enjoyed immediately. If leftovers are needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat with a splash of water or extra sauce to prevent the noodles from drying out.
